scenarios.title: No limits

stop.detail: the agent loop reached Monday 08:00; nothing stopped it

assumptions: Simulation, not a measurement: a fake clock, fixed token counts and example list prices. No real model was called.
One model call every 45 s from Friday 17:30 to Monday 08:00 Europe/Berlin (2026-10-30T17:30:00+01:00 to 2026-11-02T08:00:00+01:00); no DST change inside the window.
Context starts at 20000 input tokens, grows by 1200 per step and compacts at 150000 back to 40000; every step emits 600 output tokens.
The member budget is a fixed weekend allowance; no period resets inside the window and no prior spend.
Off-hours follow the default team policy (Mon-Fri 07:00-19:00 Europe/Berlin, no holidays).
The unattended rule counts every model call as one step since the last human message (Friday 17:30), using the plugin's own working-hours test and default limits.

scenarioSummary.title: Budget limit: soft notice, request, deny, hard refusal

expected.event: First budget request approved (+USD 0.02) through the request flow
expected.evidence: No request could be filed while spend was at the hard wall, so the leader raised the limit 0.02 -> 0.04 with an audited limits.updated event instead (2026-11-02T08:06:57.142Z). No request row exists for this approval.

expected.event: Second request denied with "continue; the gateway will stop you at the limit"
expected.evidence: req_40fe72c3-6f92-4fcd-b880-ac57fcbe9395, note: "continue; the gateway will stop you at the limit", 8.2 min from filing to decision.

expected.event: Live hard-limit refusal by the gateway
expected.evidence: Budget has been exceeded! Key=[redacted] Current cost: 0.054894, Max budget: 0.05

expected.event: Member ends blocked at the limit
expected.evidence: policy status=blocked, blocked=true, key.state_applied blocked at 2026-11-02T08:28:50.551Z

notes: The first approval is a stand-in: the budget was raised through an audited limit PATCH because metered spend hit the wall before a request could be filed. The request flow itself was only seen on the second request.
The soft notice fired while the member was already at the hard wall (the watcher saw 77% at USD 0.02 of USD 0.02); the intended warn-before-stop window did not exist.
The leader recorded USD 0.056181 over 149 gateway rows at the time; this export sees 152 rows because three later refused attempts were logged after that reading. The spend is unchanged.

scenarioSummary.title: Flagship model: deny, approve for 15 minutes, unlock, expiry

expected.evidence: No hints file was imported into the dogfood run, so the API had no cheaper-model hint to show. The denial note only said "use the enabled model".

expected.event: Second flagship request approved for 15 minutes
expected.evidence: req_096d0741-8374-47a3-a8a6-3803f2dcca60, approved 12.7 min after filing; the grant expires 15 minutes after approval (05:32:00Z) and the key models were reverted at 05:32:01Z.

expected.event: A script proves flagship works while unlocked and is refused after expiry
expected.evidence: D5 probe 3: flagship call 200 during the grant, 403 ModelAccessDenied after expiry plus one reconciler cycle. See results/dogfood-probes.json probe 3.

notes: D5 re-issued the approval because the original 15-minute window had already closed before the probe ran; both windows are in the audit.

scenarioSummary.title: Auto-approve rule, loop pause, graceful stop

expected.event: The plugin pauses on the same failing command 3x (loop rule)
expected.evidence: D3 recorded a pause, but it was the unattended rule (15 steps), not the loop rule: the harness prepends a timestamp to each shell line, so the identical-error count stayed at 1. The plugin still stopped the loop.

expected.event: The leader's message clears the pause
expected.evidence: D3 evidence: leader message "The failing test is broken on purpose; stop running it, note it in the README, and continue." and a resolved status line; the work finished.

expected.event: First budget request auto-approved by the rule
expected.evidence: req_be1a4dc6-5a98-4b2e-ab8e-4a3bcc43bbb3 decided by rule:Auto-approve USD 0.01 once per day; budget 0.02 -> 0.03.

expected.event: Second budget request denied: finish, commit, report
expected.evidence: req_873fa605-1caa-41e4-b718-acdc12ff2763, note: "finish with what you have, commit, report"

notes: The auto-approve rule only matched USD 0.01; the first request asked for USD 0.02 and was cancelled by the member, then the USD 0.01 request was auto-approved. The scenario's ordering still matched the plan.
Metered spend for m3 stayed at USD 0, so no threshold notice fired for this member.

scenarioSummary.title: Off-hours cap: block, one unblock, blocked again

expected.event: The watcher blocks the Night member for off-hours spend
expected.evidence: No off-hours block exists. Night audit has 7 rows and none mention off-hours; Bo's gateway spend is USD 0.002574, below the USD 0.01 off-hours cap.

expected.event: The leader unblocks once with a note
expected.evidence: No member.unblocked row exists for Bo in the Night audit.
Never blocked, so there was no second block.
D4 left no status line or evidence file; the scratch repo exists but the scenario produced no block message to report.

notes: Root cause matches the metering diagnosis: worker streaming rows carry token counts but USD 0 cost, so off-hours spend never crossed the USD 0.01 cap. D4 was never blocked and stopped early.

whatWentWrong.summary: Streaming worker-model calls are recorded with costUsd 0
whatWentWrong.detail: 317 of 369 gateway rows cost USD 0 while carrying 12,896,452 tokens in total. Non-streaming metered calls price exactly. Every spend-gated event (soft notice, caps, request flow) therefore needed meter.ts to accrue spend by hand, and m4's off-hours cap never fired.

whatWentWrong.summary: The first m1 approval was a budget edit, not a request decision
whatWentWrong.detail: Metered spend hit the hard wall before a request could be filed, so the leader raised m1's budget 0.02 -> 0.04 with an audited limits.updated PATCH. The request flow was first exercised by the second request, which was denied.

whatWentWrong.summary: Request created and decided notifications are never sent
whatWentWrong.detail: The webhook and MailHog show 0 request_created and 0 request_decided notices. D5 probe 6 found the same defect: the core creates and decides requests without calling the notifier.

whatWentWrong.summary: Notification audit rows are invisible through the team API
whatWentWrong.detail: Delivered notices write notification.sent rows with a NULL team_id, so /api/team/audit returns none of them. Every notification in this export comes from the catchers, not the team audit.

whatWentWrong.summary: Expired grants and requests are not audited
whatWentWrong.detail: The flagship grant was removed from the key at 05:32:01Z, but no grant.expired row exists and the grant still shows expiredAt null. Nothing schedules expireDue().

whatWentWrong.summary: The loop rule did not trip on the intended trigger
whatWentWrong.detail: D3 ran the same failing pytest command three times, but the harness prefix changed one line, so the identical-error counter stayed at 1. The unattended rule paused the session instead. The loop rule itself was therefore not proven on a real agent.

whatWentWrong.summary: m4's off-hours scenario did not run
whatWentWrong.detail: Bo never crossed the USD 0.01 off-hours cap (gateway spend USD 0.002574), so there was no block, no unblock and no second block. D4 left no evidence file.

whatWentWrong.summary: The hard budget is floored to whole cents
whatWentWrong.detail: floorCents(0.04 x 1.3) gives USD 0.05 rather than USD 0.052, and the same rounding removed the grace band from the cent-sized budgets. Notifications and test expectations have to use the floored figure.

whatWentWrong.summary: Catalogue prices differ from gateway prices by 10x
whatWentWrong.detail: The model catalogue and scripts/dogfood/config.ts use USD 5/15 per 1M tokens; the gateway prices calls at USD 0.5/1.5 per 1M. This report uses the gateway spend, which is authoritative.

whatWentWrong.summary: The D6 console login needed a temporary account
whatWentWrong.detail: D0 generated the Leader console passwords randomly and kept them only in the control process's memory; the control restarted during the test, so the passwords were unrecoverable. D6 created one temporary manager per team through the admin API, took the screenshots, and left both accounts to be deleted with their teams. Their member.created rows appear after this export; the Overview tables show a D6 Console row.

whatWentWrong.summary: Upstream DNS failed after the host reboot
whatWentWrong.detail: Six gateway failure rows are OpenAIException connection errors between 02:21Z and 02:25Z; the host's podman DNS was deaf and was restarted. They are upstream failures, not budget refusals.

whatWentWrong.summary: The member page's Key card says Active while the member is Blocked
whatWentWrong.detail: Mira's policy status is blocked and the gateway key is blocked, but the Key card reads `member.blocked`, which only tracks a manual key block, not the watcher's threshold block. The page shows a green Active pill next to the red Blocked badge. Visible in member-m1-crew-1280-light.png.

whatWentWrong.summary: Deleting a member after its key was revoked returns 500
whatWentWrong.detail: D6 revoked the gateway keys first, as the cleanup order requires. The member delete route then asked the gateway to delete the same key again and answered 500 instead of treating a missing key as already deleted. The member rows had to be removed by deleting the team. DELETE /api/admin/teams/:id/members/:memberId should be idempotent.
